guide.description: xargs <cmd> takes whitespace-separated tokens from stdin and runs <cmd> once per token, appending that token as an extra argument each time. It's how you turn a list of things (produced by any earlier command in this course) into repeated invocations of another command — the capstone move that ties a pipeline of text-processing tools to command execution.

examples.cmd: echo a b | xargs echo got:
examples.note: echo got: runs once per token, with the token appended

exercises.title: One command per token
exercises.task: Echo 'ada grace alan', then pipe it into xargs echo user: so each name is printed on its own line, prefixed with 'user:'.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: xargs runs the command once per whitespace-separated token from stdin
echo ada grace alan | xargs echo user:

criteria.label: One echo per name, prefixed with user:

check.expected:
user: ada
user: grace
user: alan

exercises.expectedOutput:
user: ada
user: grace
user: alan

exercises.title: Chain cut into xargs
exercises.task: Pull the id column (1st field) from users.csv with cut, then pipe it into xargs echo id: — notice the header row 'id' gets prefixed too, since xargs doesn't know it's special.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: cut -d, -f1 users.csv gives you the id column, one value per line, including the header
Pipe that into xargs echo id:

criteria.label: Every id, including the header, prefixed with id:

exercises.title: Chain three commands into xargs
exercises.task: Pull the status codes from access.log with awk, sort them with -u to drop duplicates, then pipe the unique codes into xargs echo status:.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: awk '{print $1}' access.log | sort -u gives the unique codes, same as the sort lesson
Pipe that into xargs echo status:

criteria.label: Each unique status code, prefixed with status:

exercises.title: Put it together: grep, awk, xargs
exercises.task: Grep for the 404 lines in access.log, pull the HTTP method (2nd field) with awk, then pipe that into xargs echo method:.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: Chain grep, awk, and xargs — all three you already know
grep 404 access.log | awk '{print $2}' | xargs echo method:

criteria.label: GET printed twice, once per 404 line, prefixed with method:
